state:
**Goal `goal-closeout`, Stage 4 (finished in place) is under way.** Stage 3 is done: `docs/agent/goal-decisions.md` names every goal in front of `goal-closeout`.

Each `Core\Task` child is held to its request's memory ceiling, and its 1 MiB stack reservation is charged while it runs (`rule:concurrency/a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled`). At the default 256 MiB ceiling, a request can have about 250 tasks waiting at once. The floor's hostile cases now fit that: groups nest 100 deep, and `Core\Time`'s sleeping fan-out runs with `limit: 100`. `tests/hostile/lang/concurrency/core-task-all-a-fixed-set-of-tasks/01-a-group-that-nests-into-itself.nvs` ends on the 100,000-deep nesting, declared `ends-early 4 FATAL`.

A limit a child reaches now stops its caller as a `FATAL` (`rule:errors/on-limit`). Before, the group handed it up as a throw a `catch` could take, and the program carried on past its memory limit. `Ctx::take_fatal` (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/error.rs`) is how the group reads it, and `Outcome::Fatal` (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/host.rs`) carries it. Pinned by `a_child_s_fatal_is_the_group_s_fatal_and_never_a_throw` in `crates/nvs-host/src/group.rs`.

**The floor check `proofs: lang:concurrency` is still red** on three attacks that keep hundreds or thousands of tasks waiting at once. They passed before only because a child's limit could be caught. `Core\Task` and `Core\Time` are green, with `Core\Task`'s perf re-measured.

**The tradeoff the user should hear:** under the default 256 MiB ceiling, a `Core\Task::map` over a few hundred elements that each wait on I/O stops with `FATAL` unless it passes `limit:`. The rule says to charge the whole reservation. Charging less is a rule change, not a session's call.

`[limits] max_tasks` is still read by nothing (`crates/nvs-config/src/default.toml` says so), and no gap owns that.

The floor check `the latest CI run on main succeeded for the code HEAD holds` is red only because `main` is many commits ahead of `origin/main`, and the loop never pushes (module doc of `tools/nv/cmd/ci-green.ts`). A person has to push, so no session can close it.

`bun nv owners --closes goal-closeout` still names 53 gaps: `nvs-host` (1), `nvs-lsp`, `nvs-runtime` and `nvs-stdlib` the largest, plus `nvs-types`, `editors/vscode` and `website`. Stage 4 stops on `BLOCKED` only for "too large", as the goal's § *Stage 4* defines it.

items.text: **The three lang:concurrency attacks fit the per-task stack charge** — `rule:concurrency/a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled` charges 1 MiB per waiting task, so each stops `FATAL` at 256 MiB: `tests/hostile/lang/concurrency/a-child-s-throw/01-a-group-where-every-task-fails.nvs:1`, `tests/hostile/lang/concurrency/core-task-map-one-task-per-element/01-a-map-over-everything-it-will-take.nvs:1` (about 8 GB charged) and `tests/hostile/lang/concurrency/no-colouring-i-o-just-waits/01-waits-piled-up-until-nothing-can-run.nvs:1` (about 270 MB). Give each fan-out a `limit:`, or move the widest step last as `ends-early <step> FATAL`, as `core-task-all-a-fixed-set-of-tasks/01-a-group-that-nests-into-itself.nvs` now does. `bun nv proofs --verify --group lang:concurrency` is the check, after `bun nv verify` rebuilt the pipeline's `nvs`.

**A task that never waits is stopped at its group's deadline** — gap `a-task-that-never-waits-outlives-its-groups-deadline`, `rule:concurrency/limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds`: `crates/nvs-host/src/group.rs:605` (`arm_deadline`) arms a reactor timer that a child looping without a call never lets fire, and the poll reads only the tree's word, `crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/safepoint.rs:59` (`share_safepoint_with`). It needs a per-group stop that a poll can read. First decide whether that is Stage 4's "too large". `tests/hostile/core/Task/all/03-tasks-that-never-wait.nvs` carries the gap's marker.

**`[limits] max_tasks` bounds the tasks a request has in flight, or the key is struck** — no gap yet: `crates/nvs-config/src/default.toml:75` documents it as read by nothing. With the stack charge in place, the memory ceiling already bounds in-flight tasks, so striking the key may be the simpler answer. `rule:security/isolate-budget-is-the-trees` is what it was for.
